svg.title: 3. Scenario: an Availability Zone fails
svg.text: Timeline (typical numbers, measure your own in a game day)
Scenario: AZ b goes bad at 20:14 on a Friday
Each AZ normally carries a third of the traffic at no more than 66% utilisation, so two AZs can carry all of it.
Red: lost with the AZ. Green: what takes over.
AZ b starts dropping packets and adding 2 s of latency. Not a clean outage:
instances still pass some health checks. p99 checkout latency jumps.
ALB marks the worst targets unhealthy, but gray failure flaps. Zonal autoshift
(or an on-call zonal shift) sets AZ b to 0% for the ALB. Errors stop here.
Aurora sees the writer is unreachable and promotes the reader in AZ a.
RDS Proxy holds client connections, so pods see a pause, not a storm of errors.
ElastiCache Multi-AZ promotes the replica in AZ c. Cart reads miss cache for
a few seconds and fall back to DynamoDB, which never noticed: it is regional.
Nodes in AZ b go NotReady. With tolerationSeconds: 60 the pods are evicted
fast instead of after the default 300 s. Karpenter starts nodes in AZ a and c.
All replicas are running in two AZs. HPA had already scaled the survivors from
66% to ~95% CPU. No orders lost: checkout writes retried with the same key.
AZ recovers. End the shift, let Karpenter consolidate, check Aurora replica lag
and rebalance. Write down how long each step took, then shorten it.
